test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 09 Sept, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: 9 men can complete a piece of work in 16 days, while 5 women can do it in 18 days. In how many days can 2 women and 4 men complete the work?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__
Total work is constant, equating work done by men and women:

9M × 16 = 5W × 18 ⇒ 144M = 90W ⇒ M ÷ W = 5 ÷ 8

Let efficiency of 1 Man = 5 units/day, 1 Woman = 8 units/day.

Total work = 9 × 5 × 16 = 720 units.

Required time = 720 ÷ (4M + 2W) = 720 ÷ (20 + 16) = 720 ÷ 36 = 20 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 20 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

9 men complete the work in 16 days.

5 women complete the work in 18 days.

 **Person** **Days** **Total Work** **Efficiency**
 9 Men 16 144 9
 5 Women 18 8
**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of 9 men = 9 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of 1 man = 9 ÷ 9 = 1 unit/day

⇒ Efficiency of 5 women = 8 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of 1 woman = 8 ÷ 5 = 1.6 units/day

⇒ Combined efficiency of 4 men and 2 women = (4 × 1) + (2 × 1.6) = 4 + 3.2 = 7.2 units/day

⇒ Time required = Total Work ÷ Combined efficiency

⇒ Time required = 144 ÷ 7.2 = 20 days

**∴ The correct answer is 20 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Chain Rule (MDH Concept)

If M₁ persons can do W₁ work in D₁ days working H₁ hours a day, then M₁ × D₁ × H₁ ÷ W₁ = M₂ × D₂ × H₂ ÷ W₂.

Work and Efficiency Relation

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken. If the ratio of time taken by A and B is x:y, then the ratio of their individual efficiencies is y:x.

Wages and Work

Wages are always distributed in direct proportion to the work done. If the time spent by all workers is the same, wages are distributed in the exact ratio of their individual efficiencies.
